names: Pier 48 Sheds A, B and C
summary: A 1928-30 reinforced-concrete finger pier with two Tudor/Gothic Revival transit sheds around an open 'valley', the southernmost contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District. The Mission Rock entitlements call for a Secretary of the Interior's Standards rehabilitation (261,000 gsf of production, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses); its planned anchor tenant Anchor Brewing closed in 2023, and today the pier is leased to the Giants' China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and events.

milestones.text: Plans for Pier 48 completed under Chief Engineer Frank G. White of the Board of State Harbor Commissioners
Concrete bulkhead wharf completed by Healy-Tibbitts Construction Company
Transit Sheds A and B completed (1929-30) by L.M. King; substructure built 1928-29
Outer end decked over and connecting Shed C built between Sheds A and B (1937-38)
Fire destroys Shed C and the eastern third of Sheds A and B
Destroyed sections reconstructed in steel framing and plywood (1999-2000)
Listed as a contributor to the Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District on the National Register
Anchor Brewing announced as anchor tenant for a 200,000 sq ft brewery in the pier, with output to rise from 180,000 to 680,000 barrels a year
Historic Resource Evaluation for the Seawall Lot 337 and Pier 48 EIR completed (VerPlanck)

Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA, which includes the rehabilitation of Pier 48, and a 10-year Pier 48 lease to China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events (Resolutions 18-03, 18-10)

Board of Supervisors approves the Pier 48 lease (Resolution 43-18, File 180093): base rent $55,416.47 a month April to September and $2,916.67 a month October to March, plus 66% of parking gross revenues, ten-year term
Port issues a Request for Interest for public-oriented uses of 13 historic piers from Pier 35 to Pier 48; responses due October 31, 2018
Phase 1 submittal keeps Pier 48 as interim event parking for 750 to 1,000 cars
Anchor Brewing announces it is ceasing operations after 127 years
Anchor Brewing bought by Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya, who says he will reopen it at its Potrero Hill plant on De Haro Street (no Pier 48 plan mentioned)

facts.value: Port of San Francisco (Board of State Harbor Commissioners when built)
1928-30; Shed C 1937-38; eastern third and Shed C rebuilt 1999-2000 after a 1996 fire

Sheds and bulkhead buildings by Board of State Harbor Commissioners engineers H.B. Fisher and B.P. Hudspeth under Chief Engineer Frank G. White; Tudor/Gothic Revival bulkhead buildings matching Pier 45
Healy-Tibbitts Construction Company (bulkhead wharf); L.M. King (transit sheds)
Contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District (listed 2006); California Historical Resource Status Code 1D
5.84 acres (HRE); 261,700 sq ft / 6.01 acres in the Design for Development parcel table
Pier substructure 369 ft wide, 610 to 635 ft long; bulkhead wharf 53 ft by 500 ft; a planned 1,200-ft pier was shortened to 623 ft because of a mud-filled 'valley' 800 ft offshore
Two parallel transit sheds (A and B) on either side of an open-air 'valley' with remnant Belt Line Railway spur tracks, joined at the outer end by Shed C; berthing on three sides
261,000 gsf of light industrial, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses under the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (HRE); the EIR project table gives 242,500 gsf
Production and 'other' uses only under the Design Controls permitted land use table; residential, commercial, retail and parking-garage uses not permitted

Interim parking and special events under a 10-year lease to China Basin Ballpark Company, LLC (Giants affiliate); marketed by Giants Enterprises as a 200,000+ sq ft venue for up to 10,000 people, 24 Willie Mays Plaza
750 to 1,000 spaces, pending demand and valet operations (2019 Phase 1 submittal)

Not rehabilitated; no Phase Submittal including Pier 48 found. The DDA notes a rehabilitation may proceed 'based on' progress of the rest of the project and that historic tax credits are being explored
Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48 as part of the Mission Rock project

open_questions: Whether the 2018 ten-year China Basin Ballpark Company lease was later amended or replaced: a five-year interim lease covering Seawall Lot 337 parking and Pier 48 sheds is described on a secondary site (citizenportal.ai) but the Port memo behind it was not located.
Any rehabilitation cost estimate or seismic/substructure study for the pier: none found in the Port memos read.
Responses to the 2018 historic piers RFI that named Pier 48: the response bundles were not read.

No source states that the Pier 48 brewery plan was formally cancelled; the inference rests on Anchor's 2023 closure and its 2024 buyer's stated Potrero Hill plan. The repo's status.csv says the buyer 'will not reopen an SF brewery', which contradicts the May 2024 reporting; flagged in the PR.
Whether the Port Commission Resolution 18-10 rent-credit terms for capital repairs were ever exercised.
Images: no rendering of the entitled rehabilitation is hosted; none appears in the public-record documents read (the 2013 Anchor Brewing scheme was never published as a Port or Planning figure).
